=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md:8,74 | severity=critical | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The 8-phase bundle cap is counted differently in implement-plan-ai (all declared phases) than in .claude/commands/audit-plans.md line 40 (only the phases still missing for a PARTIAL plan).
  WHY: A bundle that /audit-plans certifies at 8 or fewer phases can exceed 8 under /implement-plan-ai's count, so the hand-off hits its own "stop and ask" gate. Severity disagreement: MAJOR (sonnet, minimax, glm) vs NIT (luna). I used the highest, MAJOR, which has no critical equivalent, so the severity label here is normalised to the top of the scale. Same text in the workflow-templates copies.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:34-35 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The in-flight footprint item (b) and the set-aside rule still assume one singular "source plan" per tracking issue, although a bundle tracking issue can now cover up to 3 plans.
  WHY: Only one plan doc is read, so the other bundled plans' files are left out of the footprint and an overlapping candidate can pass the conflict gate. Other bundled members may also not be set aside as in flight. Severity is MAJOR for all reviewers. Line 35 was cited by sonnet and minimax only. Same text in the workflow-templates copies.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: PR description promises 5 new contract tests that "pin the bundle rules, the output block, the single-dispatch rule, and live/template parity for implement-plan-ai.md and implement-plan-claude.md"
  expected_change_site: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py:105-114 (test_implement_plan_ai_dispatches_a_bundle_once) asserts "more than 8 phases in total", the implementation-side phrasing, and not the PARTIAL-aware rule; no test cross-checks the phase-counting rule between implement-plan-ai.md and audit-plans.md, and none pins the PARTIAL-aware counting at audit-plans.md line 40
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md:8,74 (identical copy in workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: implement-plan-ai counts "more than 8 phases in total" with no PARTIAL adjustment, while audit-plans step 6 (line 40) counts only the phases still missing for a PARTIAL plan.
  WHY: A bundle the audit certifies at 8 or fewer phases can total more than 8 declared phases, for example 8 versus 11. The hand-off then hits its own "stop and ask which plans to drop" gate.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:34-35 (identical copy in workflow-templates/.claude/commands/audit-plans.md) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Footprint item (b) and the in-flight rule speak of one "source plan" per tracking issue, but a bundle now has up to 3 plans behind one tracking issue.
  WHY: A later audit may read only one plan doc, so the other plans' files are left out of the footprint. A bundled member that is not the first-named plan may be recommended again.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: In implement-plan-ai, count phases the same way as /audit-plans step 6. In audit-plans (b) and the in-flight rule, say "the plan(s) a tracking issue names". About 4 lines per file, mirrored in the templates. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md:8,74 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The 8-phase cap is counted differently from .claude/commands/audit-plans.md line 40, which counts only the missing phases for a PARTIAL plan. The bundle output example (audit-plans.md line 107) and changelog.d/audit-plans-bundles.md line 9 also drop the PARTIAL rule.
  WHY: A bundle certified by /audit-plans can exceed 8 under /implement-plan-ai's count, for example 8 versus 11, so the user is asked to drop plans they were told could ship together. The reverse is also possible: the orchestrator may count declared phases and ship more PRs than the cap intended.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:34-35 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The in-flight footprint rule ("the project's source plan", "that plan doc") and the set-aside rule ("itself the source plan of an in-flight project") assume one source plan per tracking issue, but step 6 (lines 38-41) allows up to 3 plans.
  WHY: Only the first plan doc is read, so overlapping candidates can pass the conflict gate and the orchestrator ships conflicting PRs. Other bundled plans could also slip through the set-aside rule.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: PR description promises 5 new contract tests that "pin the bundle rules, the output block, the single-dispatch rule, and live/template parity for implement-plan-ai.md and implement-plan-claude.md" | Expected change site: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py | Evidence of absence: tests/test_audit_plans_command.py:105-114 asserts "more than 8 phases in total", and no test pins or cross-checks the PARTIAL-aware counting, so the two gaps above have no contract test | SEVERITY: MAJOR | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md:8,74 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The audit counts only the missing phases for a PARTIAL plan toward the 8-phase cap, but the hand-off command counts every declared phase.
  WHY: For example, a PARTIAL plan with 5 declared phases and 3 complete counts as 2 in the audit but 5 in the hand-off. The hand-off then stops to ask which plans to drop.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:34 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The footprint instructions read only each tracking issue's singular "source plan", but one tracking issue can now reference multiple bundled plans.
  WHY: The future files of the other bundled plans are omitted from the footprint, so a candidate overlapping them can pass the conflict screen while the bundle is in flight.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: NONE. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 0
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-ai.md:8,74 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The two commands count the same 8-phase cap differently: audit-plans.md line 40 counts only the missing phases for a PARTIAL plan, while implement-plan-ai counts all declared phases. The workflow-templates mirrors have the same contradiction.
  WHY: A bundle certified at 8 phases totals 11 declared phases, so /implement-plan-ai's own gate rejects the hand-off the audit produced. The contract tests pin both contradictory texts, which locks the mismatch in.
- .claude/commands/audit-plans.md:34 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Footprint item (b) still assumes one source plan per tracking issue ("that plan doc"), although bundles now cover up to 3 plans.
  WHY: For a bundled project whose waves have not yet produced PRs, the footprint omits the other plans' touched files. A candidate overlapping only those files passes the merge-conflict gate and causes a file collision.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
